solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: British criminal gang let out — in retrospect, a disaster waiting to happen (8)

indicatorNotes.in retrospect: looking back, so the assembled letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a mob is a criminal gang
to emit is to let out

annotation.surface: A British gang is released from prison, and looking back, everyone should have seen the trouble coming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as released from jail, but it is EMIT, and 'in retrospect' is not a comment on hindsight but the order to read everything backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A time bomb, figuratively, is a situation bound to end in disaster later.

entries.clue: Centre backed arrests regularly dividing parts of Ireland (8)

indicatorNotes.backed: backed means moved backwards, so the whole assembly is reversed
indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at a regular interval: the even letters of arrests
indicatorNotes.dividing: RET sits between the two parts of Ireland, dividing them

blocks.note: ROI = Republic of Ireland, one part
NI = Northern Ireland, the other part

annotation.surface: A political centre is somehow backing arrests along a divided Ireland's border.
annotation.walkthrough: Ireland splits into two abbreviations, NI for Northern Ireland and ROI for the Republic of Ireland, and the letters from 'arrests' go between them before the whole thing is turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the inside or middle part of a thing, as in the interior of a country.

entries.clue: Infuriate former partner according to judges after losing case (10)

indicatorNotes.after: the judges' letters come after the others
indicatorNotes.losing case: the case of a word is its outside letters, so RATES loses its first and last

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
RATES (judges, assesses) without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone angers an ex by quoting what the judges said once the lawsuit was lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing case' sounds like a lawsuit lost, which fits the judges; in fact it strips the outside letters from RATES.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to make someone intensely annoyed.

entries.clue: Weird light has somewhat visible border? (10)

indicatorNotes.has: LAND has the other letters around it
indicatorNotes.border: OUTISH forms a border round LAND

blocks.note: OUT = visible (the stars are out), and -ISH = somewhat
to light (on) is to land, as a bird alights

annotation.surface: A strange light is seen, faintly visible along a frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a glow, but it is the verb, as in a bird lighting on a branch. Out means visible as stars are out at night.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: strikingly strange, as if from some far-off foreign land.

entries.clue: Adopts arguments introduced by book as an alternative (7)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: the other letters come first, introducing the arguments

annotation.surface: Someone takes on a set of arguments first put forward in a book, offering them as another view.
annotation.walkthrough: ROWS here rhymes with cows: quarrels, not lines.
annotation.definitionFit: To borrow an idea or custom is to adopt it.

entries.clue: Shop intended to give away carpet (4)

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to berate them; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: A shop meant to hand out rugs for free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is to haul them up and scold them, which makes it BERATE, taken out of DELIBERATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A short form: the delicatessen is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared food.

entries.clue: Bend initially to leap in the air (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of the word it follows

annotation.surface: An instruction to bend down first and then spring upwards.
annotation.walkthrough: CURVET is a riding term: a horse's controlled leap.
annotation.definitionFit: A curvet is a leap, a horse's jump with forelegs raised, and to curvet is to make one.

entries.clue: Repartee could turn into something fruitful? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.could turn into: the letters of REPARTEE could be turned into something else

annotation.surface: Witty banter might end up producing something worthwhile.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruitful' pretends to mean productive, as good conversation can be; the question mark admits it means literally bearing fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: A pear tree bears fruit, so it is literally fruitful.

entries.clue: Open University study halved proposal (8)

indicatorNotes.halved: only half of READ is kept

annotation.surface: A plan to cut half of an Open University course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open University' is the famous British distance-learning institution, which is exactly why the surface glues the two words together; they must be split into OVERT and U.
annotation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening proposal or approach, as in peace overtures.

entries.clue: We hear continuous sound (6)

indicatorNotes.We hear: what we hear, not what is written, signals a word that sounds like another

blocks.note: straight = continuous, as in five wins straight

annotation.surface: A voice notes a steady, unbroken noise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Continuous sound' reads as one steady hum; split it, and sound is the noun for a channel of sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of sea, which is what a strait is.

entries.clue: Order around my relations again (4,2,4)

blocks.note: My! and Lord! are both exclamations of surprise
to do something over is to do it again

annotation.surface: Someone bosses their relatives about once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My relations' reads as my family; instead 'my' is an exclamation, LORD, and 'relations' is the crossword's IT.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to behave like a lord towards others, bossing them about.

entries.clue: Lead character in Greek writer’s play (4)

annotation.surface: The leading role in a Greek author's drama.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead character' looks like a stage role, fitting the play; 'writer's' is the setter saying 'I have', I'VE, and 'play' is slack in a rope.
annotation.definitionFit: Give and play both mean slack or looseness, as in a rope with some give.

entries.clue: Presenter reportedly once had sex with failed actress (10)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as it is reported, spoken, so a word that sounds the same
indicatorNotes.failed: the letters of ACTRESS have gone wrong

blocks.note: to know someone was once, in biblical English, to have sex with them

annotation.surface: Tabloid gossip that a TV presenter once slept with an actress whose career flopped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a tabloid headline; 'once' marks the old biblical sense of KNEW, which the ear turns into NEW.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person who reads the bulletins on radio or television.

entries.clue: Talk about cut beginning to affect crime checks (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of affect
indicatorNotes.checks: THEFT checks, holds back, the A inside it

blocks.note: theft is a crime; its F and T part round the A

annotation.surface: A discussion about how cuts at the start will hinder crime-fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checks' is a verb meaning holds: THEFT holds the A. CHEW THE FAT is informal for a long relaxed chat.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for chatting at length about nothing much.

entries.clue: Racer needs moped refurbished (5,5)

indicatorNotes.refurbished: done up anew, so the letters are rebuilt

annotation.surface: A would-be racer needs their moped done up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needs' looks like the link between definition and wordplay; it is half the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A speed demon is someone who races about, always going too fast.

entries.clue: Get used to holiday home (5,2)

annotation.surface: Settling in at a holiday cottage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holiday home' reads as one thing, a cottage, but must be split in two.
annotation.definitionFit: To break in something new, like boots or a horse, is to get it used to use.

entries.clue: Low bar having nothing to justify it (8)

blocks.note: bar = except, less, as in ten less two

annotation.surface: A seedy bar that has no excuse for existing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low bar' suggests a dive, or a standard set low; both words are split, and 'bar' is the preposition meaning except.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: groundless, unfounded, like a charge made without evidence.

entries.clue: I’m not sure what to say out of respect for legal argument (7)

indicatorNotes.out of: ER is taken out of DEFERENCE

blocks.clueFragment: I’m not sure what to say
blocks.note: er is the noise of someone lost for words; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: A speaker hesitates to respond out of politeness toward a legal argument.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole opening phrase stands for one hesitation noise, ER.
annotation.definitionFit: The case argued in court on behalf of the accused.

entries.clue: Person choosing to have 100 plus soldiers promoted for protection (8)

indicatorNotes.promoted: moved up, and in a down clue up means to the top: COR goes to the front

blocks.note: a SELECTOR chooses a team; its tail COR is the 100 plus soldiers, leaving SELET in front
C = 100 in Roman numerals, plus OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers
cycling indicator: the COR at the end of SELECTOR moves to the top

annotation.surface: A team selector likes to promote a hundred soldiers to guard duty.
annotation.walkthrough: SELECTOR happens to end in C and OR, the 100 and the soldiers, so 'promoted' lifts that tail to the top of the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A corselet is a piece of body armour, worn for protection.

entries.clue: Prominent story central to article set in stone (7)

indicatorNotes.central to: LIE goes in the centre of AN
indicatorNotes.set in: a jewel set in a ring sits inside it, so ALIEN is set inside ST

blocks.note: ST = stone, the weight; it goes round everything else
an is an article; it goes round the story

annotation.surface: An important tale at the heart of a piece carved in stone.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: LIE inside AN makes ALIEN, and ALIEN inside ST. ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent, most noticeable.

entries.clue: Share tweet about being adored (10)

annotation.surface: Posting a tweet about loving someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'on the subject of'; here it stirs the letters. 'Being' is a noun: an adored being.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a beloved person, a darling.

entries.clue: Dated observation failing to save author making a comeback (6)

indicatorNotes.to save: LAPSE keeps the I safe inside it
indicatorNotes.making a comeback: coming back, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a lapse is a failing; it wraps round the I between LA and PSE
the author of the clue calls themselves I

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned remark about failing to rescue a writer's comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dated' flags that ESPIAL is an archaic word; 'failing' is the noun, a lapse.
annotation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or observation.

entries.clue: Fish needing water that’s oxygenated (4)

indicatorNotes.that’s oxygenated: O, oxygen, is put into DRY

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, added inside

annotation.surface: A fish is gasping for oxygen-rich water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needing water' fits a fish on land; it is simply DRY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the John Dory is a flat-bodied sea fish.

entries.clue: Mock support and employment when on edge (3,7)

indicatorNotes.when on: the edge goes on, in front of, the employment

blocks.note: a lip is an edge, as of a cup
being in service is being employed

annotation.surface: Someone backing and working for a cause while nervous and on edge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mock' is an adjective, meaning sham, not a verb meaning to tease.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: backing given in words only, with nothing done, so a sham of support.

entries.clue: Absolutely worst acts on stage in first half (4)

indicatorNotes.first half: keep only the first half of ROUTINES

blocks.note: first four of the eight letters

annotation.surface: The very worst stage acts are all in the first half of the show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worst' is a verb meaning defeat, so 'absolutely worst' is to defeat utterly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to defeat an enemy completely, putting them to flight.

entries.clue: Angers friend involved in race relations (6)

blocks.note: to race is to fly, go very fast
Angers is a French city, so a friend there is an ami

annotation.surface: A friend's fury gets drawn into the issue of race relations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angers' looks like the verb, but it is the French city on the Loire, telling you the friend is French: AMI. 'Race relations' is a set phrase that must be broken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your kin, the people related to you.

entries.clue: Most wanted performer to launch vessel (4,4)

blocks.note: to launch something is to start it

annotation.surface: A top criminal on the run tries to launch a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most wanted' suggests a fugitive; 'vessel' and 'launch' suggest a ship, but the vessel is a pot. A star turn is the main act on a variety bill.
annotation.definitionFit: The star turn is the headline act, the performer the audience most want to see.

entries.clue: Person of great strength consumed salt (8)

blocks.note: a titan is a giant of strength

annotation.surface: A strongman eats his salt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is the chemist's sense: a compound, here one formed from titanic acid.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemist's sense: the compound formed from titanic acid is a salt.
